solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Good deal of money — Deutschmarks — flooding a German city

parts.note: pots of money is a large amount, so pots stands for a good deal of it

indicators.note: water flooding something spreads around it, so the currency letters surround the little word a

parts.note: DM is the standard abbreviation for the old German currency
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tide of old German currency washes into a city, as if money were pouring through the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flooding' sends the currency letters around the 'a' just after it, giving DAM; 'a' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Potsdam is a historic city near Berlin, capital of the state of Brandenburg.

clue.text: Meeting to ascertain ripeness of pear?

definitions.meaning: a gathering where journalists question someone
squeezing a Conference, a common English pear variety, to test whether it is ripe

explanation.surface: A meeting called to judge whether a pear is ready to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Conference is a popular British pear variety; ripeness is tested by gently pressing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A media briefing where reporters put questions to a spokesperson is a kind of meeting.

clue.text: Set up place for art exhibition with a will

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
the Tate is a group of London galleries

explanation.surface: Arranging a gallery for a show, done enthusiastically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a will' looks like 'eagerly'; it is a legal term. 'up' turns SET to TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dies testate has left a valid legal will.

clue.text: Tedious documentary's beginning and end

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the rear is the back end

explanation.surface: A boring documentary is dull from start to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form meaning dull and gloomy, close to tedious.

clue.text: New worker mother took round is treated roughly

indicators.note: round means the mother and took letters go around the new worker letters

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
led means took, as in took someone somewhere
a hand is a manual worker, as in a farm hand

explanation.surface: A new employee is shown around by a mother and ends up being treated roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To manhandle is to handle someone roughly, so the past form means treated roughly.

clue.text: Messed up: played 'Reveille' perhaps about noon

indicators.note: about means around, so the bugling word goes around the single letter

parts.note: Reveille is the morning wake-up call sounded on a bugle, so playing it is an example of bugling

explanation.surface: A soldier botches the morning wake-up call, playing it around midday instead of at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Reveille as one example of something bugled. 'about' puts BUGLED around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean done clumsily or badly; a bungled job is one that has been made a mess of.

clue.text: Heard of someone to purchase farm building?

indicators.note: heard means the word is caught by ear, so a similar-sounding word is entered

parts.note: a buyer is a person who purchases

explanation.surface: A query whether anyone has heard of a buyer for a farm building.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is a cowshed, a farm building where cattle are kept.

clue.text: TV character not investing capital, close to bankruptcy

indicators.note: investing in the old sense of clothing or surrounding, so not wraps around the capital

parts.note: taken as written
Rabat is the capital of Morocco

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A TV figure who avoids putting money in and so ends up nearly bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' reads as finance but means surrounding. Nora Batty is the wrinkled-stockinged woman in the long-running BBC sitcom Last of the Summer Wine.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a famous figure from a British television comedy series.

clue.text: One settled in mostly free country

indicators.note: settled in means the numeral comes to rest inside the shortened word
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: liberal means generous or free
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A settler arrives in a largely free land.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits history: Liberia was founded by freed American slaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a West African nation, a country.

clue.text: Dig up various parts of Leeds City (southern half) showing lack of concern

parts.note: disinter means to dig up something buried

indicators.note: various parts suggests pieces scattered in a mixed order, so they are rearranged
in a down clue the southern half of a word is its lower or last half

explanation.surface: Excavating all over Leeds city centre, with complete indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various parts of' rearranges LEEDS plus TY, the bottom half of CITY, to ESTEDLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without personal interest or involvement, in an unconcerned or impartial way.

clue.text: Oriental writer featured in The Listener

indicators.note: a piece featured in a magazine sits inside it, so the novelist goes inside the listening organ

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens
Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: An Asian author appears in the pages of The Listener, the old BBC magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener was a real BBC weekly, which disguises the plain organ of hearing; 'featured in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and easterner both describe a person from the East, especially Asia, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Some more business for a detective

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A private investigator is promised extra work.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Rebus is the Edinburgh detective in Ian Rankin's crime novels, so the answer is a name for a detective.

clue.text: Southern Thailand plane company shortened flight

parts.note: T is Thailand's international vehicle registration code

indicators.note: shortened means the final letter of the airline word is cut off

parts.note: an airline is often named as some airways, as in British Airways

explanation.surface: A Thai airline serving the south of the country cuts back its schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests aircraft, but here it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a set of steps between floors, which is the same thing as a staircase.

clue.text: Satellite observable in October only

indicators.note: something observable in the words can be seen inside them, so the answer is a run of their letters

explanation.surface: An astronomer notes that a certain moon can be seen only in one autumn month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'observable' looks like part of the astronomy story, but with 'in' it signals the letters inside 'October only'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is one of the larger moons of Uranus, and a moon is a natural satellite.

clue.text: Creature to make slow progress in cold area

indicators.note: in means the slow-progress word goes inside the cold word

parts.note: a chill is coldness
to inch is to move forward bit by bit

explanation.surface: An animal crawls slowly through a cold region.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinchilla is a small furry South American rodent, a creature.

clue.text: For 10 it's a doddle to pack quickly

definitions.meaning: an easy investigation for a detective, one solved without effort
read literally, a suitcase that you open and shut in a moment

explanation.surface: A detective finds a case simple, while a traveller packs a bag in seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' refers to the answer at 10 across, Ian Rankin's Inspector Rebus.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a legal or police matter so clear-cut it needs no real effort, and literally a suitcase opened and closed.

clue.text: Keepers of records woman itemises

parts.note: Anna is a woman's name
to list things is to itemise them

explanation.surface: A woman sets down items one by one for archivists.
explanation.definitionFit: Annalists write annals, yearly chronicles, so they keep historical records.

clue.text: Reissued cine-film of yore containing new pop song

indicators.note: containing means the rearranged letters hold the single letter inside them
a film reissued is put out again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old movie is re-released with a fresh hit song on its soundtrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reissued' rearranges CINEFILMOFYORE; 'containing' puts N inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a well-known hit recorded by Stevie Wonder, a pop song.

clue.text: Appears in topless dress, wanting drink

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its top, the first letter in a down clue

parts.note: a frock is a dress
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone turns up in a revealing outfit, looking for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is a link meaning in need of; it does no deleting.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal phrase meaning arrives or turns up, especially casually or late.

clue.text: Type of mine not left by US force

indicators.note: not means the left letter is taken away

parts.note: a limpet mine clings to a ship's hull

explanation.surface: A kind of mine the Americans did not leave behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force or momentum that drives something forward.

clue.text: Remember to make further telephone contact

definitions.meaning: to ring someone again, read as re- plus call

explanation.surface: A reminder to phone someone back.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to bring to mind and, split up, to telephone again.

clue.text: Thick pal lost in quarry

indicators.note: letters that are lost have wandered out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dim-witted friend has gone missing in a quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit dug to extract chalk is a kind of quarry, a place where stone or minerals are excavated.

clue.text: Mount galloping along

indicators.note: galloping suggests rapid, disordered movement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A horse races along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a horse; it is a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Logan in Canada is that country's highest peak, a mountain.

clue.text: World Cup captain not sporting English tie

indicators.note: not sporting, as in not wearing, means the letter is dropped

parts.note: Bobby Moore captained England to win the 1966 football World Cup

explanation.surface: A football captain fails to wear an English tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' looks like clothing; it is a verb, as in tying up a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor a boat is to fasten it with ropes, so to tie it up.

clue.text: Aromas in hot stews oddly lacking

indicators.note: without the odd-numbered letters, so only the second, fourth and later even letters remain

explanation.surface: Spicy stews that, strangely, have no smell at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like 'strangely'; it means the odd letters are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: In wine tasting, a nose is the smell or bouquet, so noses are aromas.

clue.text: Compelled to deal with big criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is forced to do business with a powerful gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only joins the two sets of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be obligated is to be bound or forced by duty, the same as compelled.

clue.text: Former model who reveals all?

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
a model who strikes poses is a poser

explanation.surface: A retired model might be someone who bares everything.
explanation.definitionFit: One who exposes something lays it bare or makes it public, so reveals all.

clue.text: A comfy place to settle in yacht — pardon?

indicators.note: settling in means coming to rest inside, so the cosy place goes inside the yacht letters

parts.note: MY stands for motor yacht before a vessel's name
a nest is a cosy place to rest

explanation.surface: Someone, offered a cosy spot aboard a yacht, says 'pardon?' as if mishearing.
explanation.walkthrough: MY is the prefix for a motor yacht, as in MY Christina.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is a general official pardon granted to offenders.
